facts.question: Is there more or less snow than on the same date last winter, and why?
notes: model values = SnowScope snow history at one height of each resort (an estimate for an area)
measured values = a snow station on the date given (one point), only where a station history exists
days with a gain of 10 cm or more = snowfall days this winter; days with a loss of 5 cm or more = melt, rain or wind

en.title: More snow than last winter in the US Northeast? 0 of 4 resorts ahead (12 November)
en.description: Is there more snow than a year ago? We compared today with 12 November last winter at 4 resorts in the US Northeast: 0 of them have more snow now, …
en.lede: Is there more snow than a year ago? We compared today with 12 November last winter at 4 resorts in the US Northeast: 0 of them have more snow now, according to our snow model. The biggest change is at Gore Mountain: 0 in (1 cm) today against 3 in (7 cm) a year ago. Comparing with last winter is fun, but the mountain only cares about the next storm.

p: Killington Resort at 2,651 ft (808 m) has 2 in (5 cm) today: the same as the 2 in (5 cm) of 12 November last winter. For this date, the usual depth is 0 in (1 cm).
At Gore Mountain (2,316 ft (706 m)) there is 0 in (1 cm) today, less than the 3 in (7 cm) of 12 November last winter. A normal year has 0 in (0 cm) on this date.
Stratton at 2,936 ft (895 m) has 0 in (1 cm) today: less than the 2 in (4 cm) of 12 November last winter. For this date, the usual depth is 0 in (0 cm).
At Okemo Mountain (2,238 ft (682 m)) there is 0 in (0 cm) today, less than the 2 in (4 cm) of 12 November last winter. A normal year has 0 in (0 cm) on this date.
We have no station with a measured history for the same date last winter in this area, so this comparison uses our snow model only.
So far this winter at Killington Resort, our model counts 0 days that added 4 in (10 cm) or more and 0 days that lost 2 in (5 cm) or more to melt, rain or wind.
This winter at Gore Mountain: 0 days gained 4 in (10 cm) or more of snow and 0 days lost 2 in (5 cm) or more to melt, rain or wind, by our model.
So far this winter at Stratton, our model counts 0 days that added 4 in (10 cm) or more and 0 days that lost 2 in (5 cm) or more to melt, rain or wind.
At this point of the winter one storm more or less makes all the difference; do not read the rest of the season from it.
Killington Resort at this height: last winter (2025-26) topped out at 25 in (64 cm) on 26 January.
Last winter (2025-26), Gore Mountain reached its peak of 33 in (84 cm) on 26 January at this height.
Stratton at this height: last winter (2025-26) topped out at 26 in (67 cm) on 26 January.

advice: A better start than last year is no promise for the holidays: watch the forecast, not only the snow already on the ground.
Model values describe an area at one height; a station measures one point. Read both before you decide.
Snow on the map does not mean a resort is open: check lifts and dates on the resort's website.
Before any off-piste or touring day, read the official avalanche bulletin (links below).
